text:
David Pastrnak is doing what he has done for most of a decade in Boston: 22 points in 17 games, 61 shots on goal, more than 20 minutes a night, and a shootout winner against Vegas on November 2. He came into the season with 420 career goals and a Rocket Richard Trophy on the shelf, and nothing about his own game says that has changed. His eight goals sit only slightly above the 6.38 his chances were worth.

The catch is around him. With Pastrnak on the ice, the Bruins have scored about 8.0 more goals than their chances deserve, and that kind of on-ice luck fades. Expect the assists to slow before the goals do.

The partnership with Pavel Zacha is getting attention (Daily Faceoff listed them among the league's elite duos), and Evolving-Hockey's numbers from last season explain why Pastrnak's line matters so much: his teammates rated in the bottom 10 percent by impact while his competition ranked in the 97th percentile. He has carried weaker linemates against top lines for a while. Our season projection still lands around 105 points.
headline: Pastrnak's points are real; the cushion isn't
